history.dynasty: Reddy kings (steps and Pushkarini tank, 1398 AD); medieval-period stone architecture with Vijayanagara-style elements; exact original construction date unclear
history.period: Ancient stone shrine; documented Reddy-king additions dated 1398 AD
history.summary: The Sikhareswara Temple stands on Sikharam, the highest peak of the Srisailam hills (about 2830 ft, around 8 km from the main Mallikarjuna temple), commanding a panoramic view of the whole Srisailam complex and the Krishna river. The Skanda Purana's verse 'Srisaila Sikharam drustva punarjanma na vidyathe' holds that even a mere sight of this peak liberates the soul from rebirth. The ancient stone structure comprises a Garbhagriha, Antaralaya and a 16-pillared Mukhamandapa, reached by 150 stone steps built by the Reddy kings in 1398 AD; a Ganesha shrine stands nearby. Coordinates here are approximate (sourced from the 'Srisailam sikharam' place listing, ~16.046 N, 78.916 E) - no precise POI geocode was found. Opening-hours reports conflict across sources - verify before travel.

name: Sikhareswara Temple
town_description: Srisailam is a temple town in Andhra Pradesh's Nandyal district, perched on a plateau of the Nallamala Hills on the banks of the Krishna river. It grew up around the Mallikarjuna Jyotirlinga shrine and functions almost entirely as a pilgrim centre, with the Srisaila Devasthanam's choultries, Haritha resorts and markets serving visitors. Nearby attractions include the Srisailam Dam and Pathala Ganga on the Krishna, making the town a blend of intense religiosity and hill scenery.

travel.airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (approx. 220 km), with taxis onward to Srisailam town.
travel.railway: Markapur Road (approx. 87 km), nearest railhead; cabs and buses onward to Srisailam.
travel.road: The temple is about 8 km by road from Srisailam town (autos and taxis from the bus stand), followed by a climb of 150 stone steps (a 30-step southern-side entry also exists).

visitor_information.best_time: October to February; mornings are best for the view and for avoiding heat.
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICTING reports (verify): one source says 4:30 AM-6:00 PM, another 6:00 AM-2:00 PM and 5:00-8:30 PM, a third 6:00 AM-8:00 PM. Entry is free.
